title: Runoff stayed low at matched bore levels in 24 Victorian catchments, but shared-year uncertainty included zero
abstract: We tested whether the runoff loss after 1997 remained at similar observed groundwater levels. We matched years within Victorian catchments by bore anomaly, rainfall and expected runoff. In 44 pairs from 24 catchments, runoff in 2010-2019 was 0.83 calibration standard deviations below 1985-1996 at matched prior-year bore levels. The 95% spatial block interval was -1.31 to -0.37. A space and year multiplier interval was -1.59 to +0.10. Tighter rain matching gave -0.58 (-1.25 to +0.01; 11 catchments). A pre-1997 placebo gave +0.06 (-0.38 to +0.52). An exploratory subset with higher same-year bore levels still had a deficit, but a subset with both higher current and prior-year levels had only four pairs and no clear result. This test goes beyond a linear groundwater slope: it compares runoff where the observed bore state overlaps across eras. The results indicate that bore level alone is an incomplete recovery indicator. They do not identify stream disconnection. Bore composition, rain-model calibration, small samples and shared year effects limit the result.
